title: WPMS/2548/2013 of M/s A and S Constructions And Electricals Vs Uttarakhand State Matsya Palak Vikas Abhikaran AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2456 of 2013
Vikram Singh Gill Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
With
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 2548 of 2013
M/s A & S Constructions and Electricals Ö Petitioner
Vs
Uttarakhand State Matsya Palak
Vikas Abhikaran & others Ö Respondents
Advocates in WPMS No. 2456 of 2013
Mr. Sanpreet Singh Ajmani, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional C.S.C., present for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary,
Advocate, present for respondent No. 4.
Advocates in WPMS No. 2548 of 2013
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Jitendra Chaudhary,
Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional C.S.C., present for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. In these two writ petitions, the issue pertains to
a particular right over the fishing pond known as ìBaur
and Haripura Reservoirî, which is situated in District
Udham Singh Nagar. The fishing rights were to be
auctioned for the year 2013-2014 in which number of
applicants applied through their sealed cover tender forms.
The bid was to be opened in favour of the highest bidder, as
per Uttarakhand Procurement Rules.

2
2. As per the condition of the bid, a bidder has to
give earnest money of `3,60,800/- before the bid was to be
given. There were other tender conditions, such as; the
applicant should submit a valid character certificate.
Admittedly, in the said bid process, the petitioner i.e. M/s
A & S Constructions has the highest bidder i.e.
`78,60,786/-. The second highest bid for a sum of
`70,00,786/- and the third bid was for a sum of
`62,05,000/-. It is not disputed that the third highest bid
of Sri Vikram Singh Gill, who is the petitioner in WPMS No.
2456 of 2013. For the sake of convenience WPMS No. 2456
of 2013 is the first petition and another WPMS No. 2548 is
the second petition, here before this Court. Also for the
sake of convenience, although the matter pertains to the
same fishing rights, but the fact which are narrated to be
stated in first writ petition.
3. While the bids were opened an objection was
raised by the petitioner i.e. Vikram Singh Gill that the bid
of M/s A & S Constructions and Electricals (petitioner in
second writ petition) was not liable to be accepted because
he had not filed an important document i.e. his Character
Certificate issued by the concerned District Magistrate and
the character certificate, which was filed by the petitioner
was not a valid character certificate, as it had expired in
the month of May 2013 itself. Therefore, it violates the
condition of the bid, particularly condition No. 8, since the
document has not been filed and its bid was liable to be
rejected and not to be considered at all.

3
4. The petitioner i.e. M/s A & S Constructions and
Electricals in its reply relied upon a judgment of this Court
where character certificate was not to be considered as a
mandatory document and concerned competent authority
gave a character certificate to the person who fulfills the
condition and such condition of character certificate was
liable to be relaxed. In the present case also the authority
concerned had given time to the petitioner i.e. M/s A & S
Constructions and Electricals to submit character
certificate by 30.09.2013.
5. In spite of giving time to the petitioner in the
second petition to submit his character certificate when the
file reached to the superior authorities for taking a
decision, a decision was taken and communicated to the
petitioner i.e. M/s A & S Constructions that for
ìunavoidable reasonsî, although he is the highest bidder,
but his bid is being cancelled and fresh bids are to be
invited vide communication dated 19.10.2013 issued by
respondent No. 2 ñ Secretary/Uttarakhand State Matasaya
Palak Vikas Abhikaran. It is this order, which has been
challenged by the petitioner in the WPMS No. 2548 of 2013
before this Court, in second petition.
6. According to Mr. Tripathi, Additional C.S.C. for
the State the relaxation regarding character certificate is
granted in favour of the petitioner i.e. M/s A & S
Constructions and Electricals, but since the Chairman who
happens to be the Honíble Minster of the Fisheries
Department, has ordered for fresh bidding, this is being
done. The documents filed to this effect are annexure Nos.

4
2 and 3 in writ petition and the noting in this regard filed
by the petitioner has not been challenged before this Court.
The noting which has been filed by the Executive Officers
reflects that in the last year contract was given for a sum of
Rupees One crore and five lakh only, but the contract left
midway and that may be the reason for this year his bid
being lower this year. Since the bid of the petitioner i.e.
M/s A & S Constructions and Electricals is the highest and
since it consumes lot of time of the authorities for taking
exercise again he recommend that contract be even in
favour of the highest bidder. The Chairman, however,
without assigning any reason ordered for fresh bidding.
7. In view of the above, the first petition (WPMS No.
2456 of 2013) is dismissed and the second petition (WPMS
No. 2548 of 2013) is disposed of with a direction that in
case, the petitioner submits a valid character certificate to
the concerned authorities i.e. respondent No. 1, or he has
already submitted a valid character certificate the lease in
favour of the petitioner shall be considered as he is the
highest bidder. In case, the authorities concerned do not
wish to grant the contract in favour of the petitioner i.e.
M/s A & S Constructions and Electricals for any reason,
they must assign reasons and then they shall be at liberty
to re-advertise fresh tender process. In view of the above,
order dated 19.10.2013 issued by respondent No. 2 is
hereby quashed.
8. The operation and effect of this order shall be
kept in abeyance for a period ten days i.e. till 20.12.2013.

5
9. Let a copy of this order be supplied to the
learned counsel for the parties within 24 hours on the
payment of usual charges.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
09.12.2013
Aswal
